subject: Recap: When AI Agents Go Off the Rails (and how observability helps)
body:
Hello First Name,

This week's 🦄 ai that works session was a deep dive into "When AI Agents Go Off the Rails: The Power of Observability"!

If you missed it, or just want to revisit the details, the full recording, code, and diagrams are now available on GitHub:
https://github.com/hellovai/ai-that-works

We covered a lot about diagnosing and understanding those tricky, non-deterministic AI agents when they start misbehaving. Here's a quick rundown:

*   **Why AI Agents are Tricky:** Traditional debugging methods often fail with AI agents because they're non-deterministic. As user expectations climb, we see more unexpected or "off-the-rails" outcomes, and our usual tools just can't keep up.
*   **More Than Just Metrics:** We explored how observability has evolved. It's moved beyond simple metrics and logs to wide event data. To truly understand complex agent decision trees and pinpoint exactly where things went wrong, robust, in-depth tracing is essential.
*   **Tracing Helps Everyone (Even AI!):** Effective tracing provides visual 'flame graphs' that help human engineers quickly spot bottlenecks and errors. Crucially, it also allows AI agents to introspect their own call stacks, query execution paths, and diagnose issues autonomously.

The big takeaway? For non-deterministic AI agents, deep and rich tracing is absolutely critical. It's not just for debugging; it's the core method to understand, diagnose, and constantly improve your systems, giving both humans and agents the power to see inside.
